{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0.0) or shows early negative signals (e.g., -0.25), as market sentiment often underestimates downside risk.",
    "Reduce forecast overshoots following sharp upward spikes (e.g., >70% from prior day) by applying a 10-15% dampening factor to avoid overcorrection.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if 3 consecutive forecasted values are above 70.0, reduce next forecast by 2-5% to align with historical mean reversion toward 65-70 range.",
    "When sentiment is neutral or positive (sentiment = 0.0), allow forecasts to trend upward but cap growth at +5% per day to avoid overestimating bullish momentum.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, reduce the forecasted peak by 5-10% if the last 5 days show declining prices or sentiment shifts downward.",
    "If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% under), adjust next forecast downward by 3-7% to reflect potential continuation of downward trend.",
    "If true outcome is significantly above forecast (e.g., >10% over), reduce next forecast by 5-10% to avoid overestimating bullish momentum, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative."
  ]
}
